Command: Forgive as You Have Been Forgiven
Summary: The forgiveness command: forgive those who wrong you, as freely as God in Christ has forgiven you.
Commandment: Forgive those who sin against you, as your Father has forgiven you.
Application: Jesus ties our forgiveness to God's with unsettling directness, and the unforgiving servant shows what happens when a forgiven person refuses to forgive.
Purpose: Forgiveness received must become forgiveness given (Matthew 6:14-15; Colossians 3:13).
Function: Forgiveness received must become forgiveness given — Jesus ties ours to God's with unsettling directness. This comes from the New Testament, not from Sinai, so the old threefold division does not apply to it. Its goal was to make forgiven people forgiving: forgive those who wrong you, as freely as God in Christ has forgiven you. The evil it addressed was the unforgiving servant's heart — forgiven much, forgiving nothing. It restrained that evil by the link itself: if you forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive yours.
